question.value: What is the width and morphology of the Fomalhaut parent-body ring at 850 um, and what origin (planet sculpting, collision remnant, shepherd planets) best explains it?

evidence.quote: These observations demonstrate that the parent body population is 13-19 AU wide with a sharp inner and outer boundary.

evidence.quote: using the Frequency Domain Mode in dual polarization with $4\times$1875 MHz bandpasses (2 in each of the sidebands)

the RMS is $\sim60\ \mu \rm Jy~\rm beam^{-1}$ (0.32 mK)

analysis_steps.goal: Estimate mm grain mass and mass loss

method.value: Optically thin emission with s~1 mm, rho~2.5 g/cc, Tg~48 K; collisional timescale

evidence.quote: We estimate the mm grain mass by assuming the ring is optically thin and comprised of grains with $s\sim 1$ mm and $\rho_s\sim2.5$ g/cc.

assumptions.value: Collisions are the main removal mechanism

evidence.quote: If collisions are the main removal mechanism of mm grains

method.value: Two planets, 1e5 massless particles, 1e8 yr integration

evidence.quote: For each run, $10^5$ massless particles are placed between $r_{inner}$ and $r_{outer}$ with a surface density profile $\propto r^{-1}$

findings_qualitative.value: Mm grains are much more tightly confined than micron grains, consistent with radiation pressure.

claims.hypothesis: What is the width of the parent body ring?
claims.experiment: Gaussian profile and sky-model fits to ALMA 850 um image
claims.finding: Parent bodies form a narrow ring 13-19 AU wide

evidence.quote: the parent body population is 13-19 AU wide with a sharp inner and outer boundary

claims.hypothesis: Which origin best explains the ring?
claims.experiment: Compare single planet, collision remnant, and shepherd planet N-body models
claims.result: Shepherd planets reproduce narrow ring; ring too cold for flyby truncation

evidence.quote: This leads us to favor shepherd planets as the explanation for the ring’s morphology.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Collision remnant of two planets and single-planet plus stellar flyby considered; ring seems too cold for flyby.

evidence.quote: Fomalhaut’s parent body population may be too cold to be explained by this mechanism.

limitations_admitted.value: Only half of the ring is observed so the ellipse cannot be reliably determined.

evidence.quote: Without the second *ansa*, we cannot reliably determine the ellipse.

referee_caveats_inferred: Model fitting is unspecified (no likelihood/priors, no visibility-domain fitting)
Mass estimate depends on assumed grain size and no opacity
Shepherd planet conclusion is not unique

reproducibility.score_reason: Data are Cycle 0 and identifiable, but imaging and model-fitting details are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Model-fitting recipe is incomplete, so numeric results cannot be reliably redone.
